citation: Brynjolfsson E, Li D, Raymond LR. Generative AI at Work. NBER Working Paper 31161
setting: Customer-support chat agents at a Fortune 500 software firm; gen-AI assistant suggests responses
measured_effect: Chats resolved per hour +0.37 on a base of 2.6 (about +14%); average handle time -3.8 min (-9%); resolution rate +1.3 pp on 82% base; agents follow 38% of AI suggestions on average (IQR 23-50%); gains about 10% in lowest-adherence quintile and about 25% in highest
model_parameter: s (field, net of in-loop checking); r (non-acceptance)
mapped_value_or_bound: s about 0.09 (handle time) to 0.12 (1-1/1.14 throughput) per AI-assisted case; 62% of suggestions not used as-is
mapping_basis: inference: throughput gain converted to per-case time saving; in-loop review is inside the measured time
daf_process_relevance: P11 donor/advisor service inquiries (closest analogue); P05
evidence_grade: A (peer-reviewed version E02; field, large n)
limitations: Single Fortune 500 enterprise-software firm; 89% of agents outside the US, mainly the Philippines; chat not phone; suggestion tool, not autonomous agent

citation: Brynjolfsson E, Li D, Raymond L. Generative AI at Work. Quarterly Journal of Economics 140(2)
setting: As E01 (published version)
measured_effect: Issues resolved per hour +15% on average; less experienced/lower-skilled workers gain in speed and quality; most experienced/highest-skilled see small speed gains and small quality declines; fewer requests to speak to a manager
mapped_value_or_bound: s about 0.13 per case (1-1/1.15)
mapping_basis: inference: as E01
limitations: As E01; heterogeneity means a skilled incumbent team gains less

citation: Dell'Acqua F, McFowland E, Mollick E, Lifshitz-Assaf H, Kellogg KC, Rajendran S, et al. Navigating the Jagged Technological Frontier. Organization Science (earlier HBS WP 24-013 / SSRN 4573321, 2023)
retrieved_via: OpenAlex record W7135096569 (abstract), resolved from SSRN DOI 10.2139/ssrn.4573321
setting: BCG consultants on 18 realistic consulting tasks inside the AI frontier and one task outside it
measured_effect: Inside frontier: 12.2% more tasks completed, 25.1% faster, higher quality. Outside frontier: AI users 19% less likely to produce correct solutions
mapped_value_or_bound: s about 0.25 on in-frontier tasks; error-rate penalty about 0.19 on out-of-frontier tasks
mapping_basis: inference: 25.1% faster read as per-task time saving before downstream checking
limitations: Experimental tasks, not production work; GPT-4 (2023)

citation: Noy S, Zhang W. Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence. Science 381(6654)
setting: Occupation-specific mid-level professional writing tasks
measured_effect: Time taken -40%; output quality +18%
mapped_value_or_bound: s about 0.40 on drafting tasks
mapping_basis: inference: drafting share of DAF processes (letters, donor replies, memos) only
limitations: Short, self-contained writing tasks; ChatGPT-3.5; online participants

citation: Dillon EW, Jaffe S, Immorlica N, Stanton C. Shifting Work Patterns with Generative AI. NBER Working Paper 33795
setting: Knowledge workers given M365-integrated gen-AI (email, meetings, writing)
measured_effect: 80% of treated workers used the tool; users spent two fewer hours per week on email; no detected shift in quantity or composition of tasks
mapped_value_or_bound: Whole-job saving bounded well below task-level savings; email share of week not given in abstract
mapping_basis: inference: field general-purpose tool supports low whole-pool saving
limitations: General-purpose assistant, not a process-specific workflow

citation: UK Department for Work and Pensions. An Evaluation of DWP's Microsoft 365 Copilot Trial (GOV.UK)
setting: Civil servants in a benefits department, Oct 2024 to Mar 2025
design: User vs comparison-group surveys with regression (SUR/OLS); interviews
measured_effect: Average 19 minutes per day saved across 8 routine tasks (SUR); 85% rated meeting-note accuracy good or very good; users report verification and double-handling overhead
model_parameter: s x a (whole-job); r (share of outputs not rated good)
mapped_value_or_bound: Whole-day saving about 19 min/day; about 15% of meeting summaries not rated good
mapping_basis: inference: 15% treated as a lower-bound rework share for summarisation outputs
daf_process_relevance: Public-sector administration analogue for P05, P11, P15
evidence_grade: B (government evaluation; self-reported outcomes, non-random comparison)
limitations: Self-reported time; volunteers and nominees, not random assignment

citation: UK Government Digital Service. Microsoft 365 Copilot Experiment: Cross-Government Findings Report (GOV.UK)
setting: Civil servants across 12+ organisations, 30 Sep to 31 Dec 2024
measured_effect: Average 26 minutes per day saved (self-reported midpoint method); drafting documents 24 min, presentations 19 min, scheduling 9 min; accuracy concerns in domain-heavy tasks
mapped_value_or_bound: Whole-day saving about 26 min/day, upper bound (self-report, no control)
mapping_basis: inference: used only as an upper whole-job bound
limitations: No counterfactual; self-report midpoints

citation: Bick A, Blandin A, Deming DJ. The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI. NBER Working Paper 32966
setting: US nationally representative survey of adults 18-64
sample: Nationally representative US samples (Nov 2024 wave for time savings)
measured_effect: Users report time savings of 5.4% of work hours on average; 1.4% of total work hours across all workers; 1-5% of all work hours assisted by gen-AI
mapped_value_or_bound: Whole-job saving among users about 0.05
mapping_basis: inference: economy-wide; DAF back office may differ
limitations: Self-reported; not process-specific

citation: Humlum A, Vestergaard E. Still Waters, Rapid Currents: Early Labor Market Transformation under Generative AI (formerly 'Large Language Models, Small Labor Market Effects'). NBER Working Paper 33777
setting: Denmark: 11 AI-exposed occupations incl. accountants, customer support, office clerks, financial advisors
design: Surveys linked to administrative records; difference-in-differences
sample: About 25,000 valid responses per survey round (115,000 invited)
measured_effect: Adopters report savings of about 3% of work hours; precise null effects on earnings and recorded hours (rules out >2%); AI chatbots created new workloads for 12% of users (8 pp new tasks), about 18% where employers run initiatives; new tasks include AI quality review and AI ethics/compliance
model_parameter: s x a (whole-job); q (new oversight work)
mapped_value_or_bound: Whole-job saving about 0.03; oversight tasks appear for 8-18% of users
mapping_basis: inference: oversight incidence is not a per-case re-review rate
limitations: Self-reported time savings; mostly general chatbots in 2023-24

citation: Eloundou T, Manning S, Mishkin P, Rock D. GPTs are GPTs: labor market impact potential of LLMs. Science 384(6702) (arXiv 2303.10130)
retrieved_via: OpenAlex record W4399848789 (metadata); arXiv abs page 2303.10130 (abstract numbers)
setting: US occupations (O*NET task exposure rubric, human and GPT-4 ratings)
design: Task-exposure classification (not a measurement of realised savings)
measured_effect: About 15% of all worker tasks could be completed significantly faster at the same quality with an LLM alone; 47-56% with LLM-powered software; about 80% of workers have at least 10% of tasks exposed, about 19% at least 50%
mapped_value_or_bound: Cost-weighted mean a between about 0.15 (LLM alone) and about 0.56 (with tooling); calibrated cap 0.60
mapping_basis: inference: exposure is potential, not realised; used only as a ceiling
limitations: Exposure, not adoption; US task mix

citation: Becker J, Rush N, Barnes E, Rein D. Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity. arXiv 2507.09089
setting: Experienced open-source developers on their own mature repositories
measured_effect: Allowing AI increased completion time by 19%; developers believed it reduced time by 20%
mapped_value_or_bound: s can be negative for experts on mature, context-heavy work; calibrated lower bound 0.00
mapping_basis: inference: domain is software, used only for the sign of the lower tail and for self-report bias
limitations: Small sample; software domain

citation: Peng S, Kalliamvakou E, Cihon P, Demirer M. The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot. arXiv 2302.06590
setting: Recruited developers implementing an HTTP server in JavaScript
measured_effect: Treatment group completed the task 55.8% faster
mapped_value_or_bound: s upper bound about 0.56 for a well-specified, self-contained task
mapping_basis: inference: upper bound only
limitations: Single well-specified task; author affiliations not checked

citation: Magesh V, Surani F, Dahl M, Suzgun M, Manning CD, Ho DE. Hallucination-Free? Assessing the Reliability of Leading AI Legal Research Tools. Journal of Empirical Legal Studies
setting: Commercial RAG legal research tools (Lexis+ AI, Westlaw AI-Assisted Research, Ask Practical Law AI) vs GPT-4
design: Preregistered evaluation on a legal query set
sample: Query count not stated in retrieved abstract
measured_effect: Tools hallucinate between 17% and 33% of the time; lower than general-purpose GPT-4
model_parameter: r (share of AI outputs needing correction)
mapped_value_or_bound: r about 0.17-0.33 for retrieval-heavy rule interpretation
mapping_basis: inference: legal research is the nearest public analogue to rule interpretation in P07/P08/P01
daf_process_relevance: P07 non-standard due diligence, P08 benefit review, P01 KYC rule checks
limitations: Benchmark queries, not production cases; 2024 tool versions

citation: Martin L, Whitehouse N, Yiu S, Catterson L, Perera R. Better Call GPT, Comparing Large Language Models Against Lawyers. arXiv 2401.16212
setting: Contract review vs junior lawyers and legal process outsourcers, ground truth by senior lawyers
measured_effect: Advanced LLMs match or exceed junior-lawyer accuracy in determining legal issues; review completes in seconds vs hours; 99.97% cost reduction
model_parameter: s (upper bound for document review); a_p
mapped_value_or_bound: Machine time near zero; human verification not included, so not used as s
mapping_basis: inference: shows the task-level ceiling; verification cost dominates in practice
daf_process_relevance: P03 complex-asset documents, P07, P13 document review
limitations: Excludes human verification time; author affiliations not checked

citation: Eddin AN, Bono J, Aparicio D, Polido D, Ascensao JT, Bizarro P, Ribeiro P. Anti-Money Laundering Alert Optimization Using Machine Learning with Graphs. arXiv 2112.07508
setting: Real-world banking AML transaction-monitoring alerts reviewed by human investigators
design: Retrospective model validation (ML triage, not gen-AI)
sample: Real-world banking dataset (size not stated in retrieved abstract)
measured_effect: Triage model reduces false positives by 80% while detecting over 90% of true positives
model_parameter: s and r for P14 alert handling
mapped_value_or_bound: Alert workload reduction up to about 0.8 of false positives, at the cost of about 10% of true positives if auto-closed, so human review of closed alerts stays
mapping_basis: inference: auto-closing is not acceptable for SAR obligations; maps to a high s on screening with a non-trivial residual review share r about 0.10
limitations: ML triage, not LLM; single bank; author affiliations not checked

citation: Bank of England and FCA. Artificial intelligence in UK financial services - 2024
setting: UK financial firms (banks, insurers, asset managers, etc.)
measured_effect: 75% of firms use AI; 55% of AI use cases have some automated decision-making, 24% of those semi-autonomous with human oversight for critical or ambiguous decisions; 2% of use cases fully autonomous; highest perceived current benefits in data/analytics, AML and fraud, cybersecurity; one third of use cases are third-party, 64% in risk and compliance
mapped_value_or_bound: Near-universal human sign-off on consequential decisions (fully autonomous 2%) supports the CAL_COMPLIANCE_FULL stress
mapping_basis: inference: share of use cases, not share of cases reviewed
limitations: Use-case counts, not volumes; UK regulated firms

citation: Choi JH, Xie C. Human + AI in Accounting: Early Evidence from the Field. Journal of Accounting Research (earlier SSRN 5240924)
retrieved_via: OpenAlex record W4410159472 (abstract; SSRN page returned HTTP 403 and was not used)
setting: AI-enabled accounting platform serving SMEs; survey of professional accountants
design: Field data plus survey plus framed field experiment
sample: 277 accountants surveyed; 79 SMEs; over 200,000 transaction records
measured_effect: GenAI adoption associated with significant productivity gains (magnitude not in retrieved abstract), reallocation from data entry to communication and quality assurance, more granular ledgers and faster month-end close; accountants selectively intervene when AI confidence scores are low; reliance on non-consensus AI recommendations raises error risk
mapped_value_or_bound: No magnitude used; supports confidence-gated (partial) review rather than 100% review in bookkeeping-like processes
mapping_basis: inference
daf_process_relevance: P02 contribution intake, P10 reconciliation, P12 receipts, P15 Schedule D data
limitations: Magnitudes not retrieved; SME bookkeeping, not fund accounting

citation: Angelova V, Dobbie W, Yang C. Algorithmic Recommendations and Human Discretion. NBER Working Paper 31747
setting: Bail decisions with algorithmic recommendations
sample: Judges in one jurisdiction (count not in retrieved abstract)
measured_effect: 90% of judges underperform the algorithm when they make a discretionary override; the other 10% outperform it in accuracy and fairness
mapped_value_or_bound: Overrides do not reliably add accuracy, so review cost is not automatically repaid by error reduction
mapping_basis: inference
limitations: Non-financial domain; predictive algorithm not gen-AI

citation: Agarwal N, Moehring A, Rajpurkar P, Salz T. Combining Human Expertise with Artificial Intelligence: Experimental Evidence from Radiology. NBER Working Paper 31422
setting: Professional radiologists with and without AI predictions
sample: Professional radiologists (count not in retrieved abstract)
measured_effect: AI predictions do not uniformly raise diagnostic quality; radiologists underweight AI; optimal design assigns cases to human or AI, rarely to human-assisted-by-AI
mapped_value_or_bound: Supports routing designs (AI-only on easy cases, human-only on hard) over assist-everything
mapping_basis: inference
limitations: Medical domain

citation: Liang W, Zhang Y, Cao H, et al. Can Large Language Models Provide Useful Feedback on Research Papers? NEJM AI 1(8)
setting: GPT-4 generated scientific feedback vs human peer review; prospective user study
design: Retrospective overlap analysis plus user study
measured_effect: 57.4% found GPT-4 feedback helpful or very helpful; 82.4% found it more beneficial than feedback from at least some human reviewers; authors advise human review remains the foundation
mapped_value_or_bound: Supports AI as a first-pass reviewer, not a replacement; no time measure
mapping_basis: inference
daf_process_relevance: P05 grant recommendation intake, P07 grantee due diligence (grant-review analogue)
limitations: Perception, not productivity; research papers not grant applications

citation: Choi JH, Monahan A, Schwarcz D. Lawyering in the Age of Artificial Intelligence. Minnesota Law Review 109
setting: Law students on realistic legal tasks with or without GPT-4
measured_effect: Large and consistent increases in speed; only slight and inconsistent quality improvement; time saved similar regardless of baseline speed (magnitudes not in retrieved abstract)
mapped_value_or_bound: Not used numerically
mapping_basis: inference
evidence_grade: A (RCT) for direction; magnitude not retrieved
limitations: Students not practitioners; magnitudes not retrieved
